title: Ask to Distill: Learning to Synthesize Data for On-Policy Distillation
abstract: arXiv:2610.27450v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) can succeed with surprisingly few training questions, motivating a view of questions as carriers of distributional knowledge transfer. How can we assess whether a newly generated question is valuable for distillation, and learn to generate better questions---without access to its correct answer? We introduce Ask-to-Distill (\method), a framework that treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes the teacher supervision they expose along student-generated trajectories. A student-initialized synthesizer is optimized using a distributional surrogate for question value, computed from a frozen student--teacher pair without reference answers, correctness rewards, or per-candidate student updates. The reward combines teacher--student disagreement with teacher probability mass on the student's candidate support, together with length and diversity controls. translated_title: 提问以蒸馏：学习合成数据用于同策略蒸馏
translated_abstract: 同策略蒸馏（OPD）仅用极少的训练问题就能取得成功，这促使我们将问题视为分布性知识迁移的载体。那么，我们如何评估一个新生成的问题对蒸馏是否有价值，并在无法获得其正确答案的情况下学习生成更好的问题？我们提出了 Ask-to-Distill 框架，该框架将合成问题视为分布引子，并优化这些问题在学生模型生成的轨迹上所引出的教师监督。一个以学生模型初始化的合成器，通过问题价值的分布性替代指标进行优化，该指标由冻结的学生-教师模型对计算得出，无需参考答案、正确性奖励，也无需针对每个候选问题更新学生模型。该奖励将师生分歧度与教师在学生候选支持集上的概率质量相结合，并辅以长度和多样性控制。所生成的问题经过过滤后……（摘要截断）
tldr: 该论文提出Ask-to-Distill框架，将合成问题视为分布引子，利用基于师生分歧等信号的分布性替代奖励（无需参考答案或正确答案）来评估并优化合成问题的价值，从而实现高效的同策略蒸馏数据合成。
en_tdlr: Ask-to-Distill treats synthetic questions as distribution elicitors and optimizes them with a distributional surrogate reward (teacher–student disagreement plus teacher probability mass) computed from a frozen student–teacher pair without reference answers, enabling effective data synthesis for on-policy distillation.
